answer: A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is proof-of-environmental-binding. Each agent must submit a verifiable real-world sensor reading before transacting—a timestamped light-spectrum capture of a glacier at dawn, where violet wavelengths dominate the scattered sky, plus a soil-sensor reading of pigment concentration. These readings are location- and time-bounded, so attackers cannot cheaply forge them at scale. A thousand fake agents need physical control of a thousand distinct sensor nodes across repeated epochs. That cost dwarfs any extractable reward, making sybil attacks uneconomical.
